cls: Hepatoprotective flavonolignan complex (milk thistle / Silybum marianum extract)
pharm: Antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and membrane-stabilizing hepatoprotectant; principal component silibinin
quick: 140 mg silymarin two to three times daily (commonly 420 mg/day)
Limited data; avoid unless clearly needed
Limited data; traditionally used as galactagogue, caution

LFTs / clinical response in liver disease
summary: Silymarin is a standardized flavonolignan complex from milk thistle (Silybum marianum) seeds, with silibinin (silybin) as the main active component. It is used as a hepatoprotective agent in chronic liver disease, toxic/drug-induced liver injury, and as supportive therapy (an IV silibinin product is used for Amanita phalloides poisoning in some countries). It is generally well tolerated. Note: silymarin is marketed as a herbal medicine/nutraceutical and is not an FDA-approved drug; dosing and evidence derive from EMA/herbal monographs and clinical use rather than an FDA label.
indications: Supportive treatment in chronic liver disease (e.g., alcoholic and non-alcoholic liver disease, hepatitis)
Supportive therapy after Amanita phalloides (death cap) mushroom poisoning - IV silibinin where available
Traditional use to support liver function and digestion

dosage.d: 140 mg silymarin two to three times daily
dosage.n: Commonly 420 mg/day total; standardized to silymarin content

admin: Take oral preparations with or after food
Use standardized extracts (silymarin content); products vary in bioavailability
For mushroom poisoning, IV silibinin is administered under specialist/poison-center guidance
Maintain alcohol abstinence in patients with liver disease
moa: Acts as a free-radical scavenger/antioxidant, stabilizes hepatocyte cell membranes (reducing toxin uptake, e.g., competing with amatoxin transport), inhibits lipid peroxidation, exerts anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic effects, and may stimulate hepatocyte protein/RNA synthesis and regeneration.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to silymarin, milk thistle, or other Asteraceae/Compositae plants (e.g., ragweed, chrysanthemum)
relative: Patients on narrow-therapeutic-index drugs (possible CYP/transporter effects)
monitor: Liver function / clinical response in liver disease

preg: Limited safety data in pregnancy; not adequately studied. Avoid unless clearly needed and benefit outweighs uncertain risk.
lact: Limited data; traditionally used as a galactagogue in some cultures. Safety in breastfeeding is not well established - use with caution.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment described; limited renal data. Generally considered low risk.
hepatic: Primarily used in hepatic disease and is generally well tolerated; no dose reduction typically required.

moderate: Substrates of CYP2C9 (e.g., warfarin) - in vitro inhibition; monitor where clinically relevant
Drugs sensitive to UGT/OATP transport - theoretical alteration in exposure
minor: Sirolimus / certain immunosuppressants - possible modest exposure changes (monitor)
Hypoglycemics - may modestly affect glycemic control in diabetics with liver disease
interactions.food: Take with or after food; food may aid tolerability
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol, particularly in liver disease
interactions.diagnostics: May contribute to improvement in elevated transaminases in liver disease (monitor LFTs)

serious: Allergic reactions in those sensitive to Asteraceae plants

monitoring: Liver function tests and clinical response in liver disease
counsel: This is a herbal/supplement product used to support liver health - it does not replace abstinence from alcohol or prescribed treatment
Avoid if you are allergic to ragweed, marigold, daisy, or chrysanthemum
Mild loose stools or stomach upset can occur and are usually transient
Tell your clinician about all medicines, especially blood thinners
Inform your clinician if pregnant or breastfeeding
pk: Gradual; clinical effect over weeks of use
Plasma silibinin tmax ~1-2 h (low oral bioavailability)
Store at room temperature, protect from light and moisture
pearls: Not an FDA-approved drug - marketed as a herbal medicine/dietary supplement; dosing/evidence per EMA/HMPC monographs and clinical practice, not an FDA label
Silibinin (silybin) is the principal active flavonolignan; oral bioavailability is low (often formulated as silibinin-phosphatidylcholine to improve absorption)
IV silibinin (Legalon SIL) is used as adjunct therapy for Amanita phalloides poisoning in several countries
Generally well tolerated; main caution is Asteraceae-family allergy and possible mild CYP2C9 effects
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it; do not double up.
overdose: No serious toxicity reported even at high doses; excess may cause GI upset and loose stools. Management is supportive.
